entry.text: ...Alright, it's simple.
(That's Félix. He owns the place, which unfortunately means he gets to tell me what to do.)
...Customer asks for something, you grab it, put it in the bag.
Check the price, set it on the till, pull the lever. That's it.
And when they pay, count it right. People get weird about their change.
[Click on an item to read its description. Drag it into the bag to add it to the purchase.]
[To ring up the total, enter the price on the till, then drag the lever down.]
[Count the customer's money, then click on the right banknotes and coins to give them their change.]
[Click on the [...] button to talk to the customer or ask them to remind or explain their order.]
[You can find this anytime in ⚙ Help.]
Let's try it out. Sell me a tin of Morley.

wrong_items.text: That's not what I asked for. Try again.

wrong_price.text: Right stuff, wrong number. Do the math again.

click.text: A tin of Morley tobacco. In the bag, on the till, then the lever.

wrong_change_under.text: Careful, short-changing is a skill. You clearly don't have it yet.

wrong_change_over.text: You're being generous. That's too much.

checkout.text: See? Easy enough.

checkout_st1.text: Okay, you figured it out, eventually.

entry.text: Round two. Paper for smoke, paper for thought. Two of one, one of the other.

wrong_items_st1.text: That's not what I asked for. Again.

options.text: This place wasn't a tobacconist before

response.text: Yeah, I opened it about a year ago. Year and a half, maybe. Came back to Larris, found the place empty, figured I'd try selling something legal for once.
You know the trope. The big world doesn't want you, so you crawl back to your quirky little hometown to complete your mandatory redemption subplot.
Anyway. Could've ended up somewhere worse than a smoke-stained counter.

options.text: What was it you asked for?

response.text: Paper for smoke, paper for thought. Two of one, one of the other.
What, riddle too hard? It's just a newspaper and two packs of rolling papers.

wrong_price.text: Want to double-check before I call the math police?

checkout.text: Well done. That's the job - sit here, sell people their little habits, read the paper if you want, and don't let the till jam. If it does, hit it.
...Some people come in more for the conversation than the cigarettes. Whether you listen or not is up to you.
That's it. I vanish now.

break.text: ...Guess I'll take a look at the news while nobody's here.

entry.text: Morning.
One pack of JCs and a lighter. The kind I won't miss if it goes overboard.

options.text: Back from the big metal boats?

response.text: Yeah. Long trip.
Should've been back Friday, but... engine acting up, weather turning, everyone getting a bit short with each other.
Heh, funny thing is... somewhere in the middle of it one of the lads goes, "Hell, if the old church organ's still going, we'll manage too."
Then I step off the boat and first thing I hear is it finally packed in.
...Funny, isn't it?
JC reds and any cheap, basic lighter.

wrong_items.text: JC reds and any cheap, basic lighter.

checkout.text: Thanks.
You don't happen to be after a little fishing boat, do you?

response.text: I'd buy it right away if money and common sense weren't involved.
Yeah. Been having trouble with those myself.
Don't think a fishing boat really fits into my life right now.
Yeah. Starting to look that way for me too.

checkout.text: Everyone keeps telling me to let mine go. They say little boats are finished and trawlers are the future.
We'll see.
Anyway. Have a good one.

entry.text: Alright, Babette. What are we in the mood for today?
Mm... the pretty Fleuries with the rose petals?
Tempting. But we just spent two hours scraping wax off pews. I think we deserve a little sin.
You're thinking what I'm thinking, aren't you?
One cigar, please. We've earned it.

click.text: ...they've got it all draped up like a dead body.
Don't say that, Lucie. I'll be very sad if our dear organ's really gone for good.
I saw the music fellas in there yesterday. They'd already pulled out some pipes.
Oh, so they already let Noose Boy out?
I'm just saying. He's sweet, but he looks like he'd pass out halfway through a rosary.

response.text: Mm. She helped us in the hospital and around the church, just... quietly. Kept her life close. We didn't even know she had a daughter...
Just one cigar, dear.

wrong_price.text: Hmm. That's not what it cost last time.

checkout.text: Thanks. You know, we only smoke together. That makes it a ritual, not a habit.
Exactly. We'll take this, say our midday prayer and sit under the sky a bit. Let the morning settle.
And hopefully no one smells temptation and gets nervous. I'd rather not fall apart mid-prayer like our poor organ.
Babette.
...Blessings, dear.

break.text: (Guess nobody's coming. Looks like I can get back to that sudoku now.)

entry.text: ...And so the daughter returns home. To the dust her mother called holy, and the stillness she mistook for peace.
Step careful. They wait to see what you'll do differently.

response.text: To see what happens, maybe.
Silence is God's first language.

entry.text: (Still the same love for fancy words, I see. And that faint smell of wine hasn't left him either.)
Mmm...
The latest paper and Fleuries, please. The mugwort blend, if the Lord still provides.

response.text: Oh, nothing specific, just an old, neurotic instrument making a scene. Even holy things tire of speaking and sometimes they... shut themselves off.
It stings, yes - you can tend and polish, care and pray, and still what you cherish may slip away. For all flesh is grass, and grass withers... and organs...
...are wood, partially. Wood is almost grass, right? Never mind, the point is clear: His word alone abides.
...Anyway, thanks God our good old repairman gets along with anything that's fallen out of tune. The organ is already in his care.
So don't frown, and don't bother your head too long about it.
Who else but Yves? Luckily still with help from Pierrick, hanging on beside him...
(I've probably heard of them before. Or maybe just feels like I have. This town's too small.)

options.text: Any plans for a temporary fix?

response.text: You think it can't just be quiet for a while? Yesterday there were no chords, and yet... people still prayed.

options.text: A bit of soundtrack never hurts

response.text: Maybe. After all, heaven never minded a little background music.

options.text: No background noise for a change

response.text: Exactly. World's loud enough already, honestly.

But the truth is... if we can't afford whatever Yves discovers inside, I'm afraid the choice won't be mine to make. There's already been some talk from higher-up about selling what's left of the organ and replacing it with a piano.
A sensible solution, I suppose. Reliable. Affordable. Easier to look after. Still... I'd hate to see it end that way.

options.text: Which holy blend are we burning today?

response.text: Mugwort Fleuries. And the news. Let it be so.

wrong_items.text: We all reach for the wrong thing sometimes.

paying.text: Ah. Coins. Notes. Prices creep up, donations crawl along.
People are generous, in theory. In practice, they need reminding what they're paying to keep alive.

checkout.text: Much obliged.
You know, I used to send someone else to fetch these for me. Then he quit smoking, selfish man, and suddenly I'm the one walking again.
But today it brought me to you, so I'm calling it a good walk.
No more words from me. Be strong and of good courage.

entry.text: Interesting. You're definitely not Félix, unless he got prettier.
He died, lucky bastard? Probably no, just playing hide and seek again.
Anyway, my name is Yves. I fix things. Instruments, mostly.
And you are?...

response.text: Oof, my wife says never trust someone whose name has funny letters in it. But maybe I should give you a chance.
Nice to meet you, Just Gail.
Sweet. I can already hear Félix cackling.

entry.text: Well, normally I'd be here for pipe tobacco. But I quit.
So nothing for me today... or maybe the news?
No. No, I don't want to know what's going on.
Hmm.
I'll take those tiny papers you roll cigarettes with. And a box of matches. Just in case.

options.text: People are already talking about the organ

response.text: Of course they are. It would've been too boring to just say it was its time. They've got their little theories.
Still. It'll play again. Can't promise a third-day rise, but I've fixed worse.
Oof, I've had enough of the work talk for today, {{name_yves}}, and it's only Monday. Mind if we change the subject?
Nope. I quit last month.
Guy from the brass quartet said smoke messes with your diaphragm. Makes it harder to hold a note.
Can't have that. I've got solos to play.
Tiny cigarette papers and matches.

options.text: You were a smoker for how long?

response.text: Long enough to forget when I started.
I let a nun stick needles in my ears twice a week. Helps with urges.
Hmm, let's see...
Cornet when I'm feeling gentle. Trombone when I'm not. Clarinet... maybe when I don't quite feel like being myself.
Suppose if it takes lungs to play, chances are I've tried it.

wrong_items.text: Creative interpretation, {{name_yves}}, but I asked for something else.

wrong_price.text: Off by a few notes. You might want to tune that till.

wrong_price_yvesAbigail.text: So my wife was right about you people with funny letters?

checkout.text: Didn't you say you quit? What's with the papers?
Oh, I just like having them on hand. I've noticed they're the kind of thing people run out of right when they actually need it.
Well, thanks for the company and enjoy the rest of the evening.
I like it when the town goes quiet. Makes me want to play flugelhorn and think about my funeral arrangements.
Catch you next time, {{name_yves}}.

entry.text: ...You're not Félix.

response.text: Hi, Abigaïl. Menthol Morleys, please.
Hi, Gail. Menthol Morleys, please.
...Fish?
Alright... Menthol Morleys, please.
(Not deaf. Just petty.)
Menthol Morleys. I did say it. Clearly.
(Not deaf. Just petty.)
Menthol Morleys. I did say it. Clearly.

wrong_items.text: I asked for Menthol Morleys. Not... whatever that is.

checkout.text: Thanks.

entry.text: Surprise. I exist again.
Shop's still standing, and so are you. See? Knew you were born for this. Natural cashier.
But that's enough heroics for today. Key's under the counter. Let's close up.

dialog.text: Old tenement building with damp stairwells, laundry lines stretched across the yard and piss in the corners, standing in a row of exact same houses in a shitty neighbourhood. Four floors, tiny flats.
When I was little, the fishmonger was there. The whole building smelled like salt and guts, but after a while, I stopped noticing. Mum never did.
Then it became a photo studio. No more fish, just chemicals, paper and whatever cologne that prickish photographer marinated in daily.
Then I was gone for a while. Came back, and the old space is a tobacco shop now. Out of everything that's been here, this smell makes the most sense.
Fish gone. Photographer gone. Just tobacco now.
Well... Tobacco, and a debt my mum forgot to take with her.
We lived above this little shop for years. It just never crossed my mind I'd end up working here. Especially not because of a debt that wasn't even mine.
Anyway... here I am. First day behind the counter.

start.text: ...Bet you can't wait for the next shift.

response.text: Perfect, I'll need your help on Friday. Key's yours.
Thought so. Still need you on Friday. Key's yours.

start.text: ...Only if you get me a typewriter.
Ha. Planning to crack those newspaper puzzles?
